questions.question: What does the BEM acronym stand for in CSS architecture?
questions.explanation: BEM stands for Block, Element, Modifier, a popular methodology for writing modular, scalable CSS.

questions.question: In the BEM methodology, how are elements and modifiers delimited in class names?
options: Elements use __ (double underscore); Modifiers use -- (double hyphen)
Elements use dot; Modifiers use comma
Elements use dash; Modifiers use slash
Elements use hash; Modifiers use colon
questions.explanation: BEM uses double underscores for elements (.card__title) and double hyphens for modifiers (.card--active).

questions.question: Why is keeping CSS selector specificity low and uniform a core best practice?
options: It prevents specificity wars, making styles easy to override and maintain across large teams
It is required for Google indexing
questions.explanation: Maintaining flat, uniform specificity avoids convoluted selector chains and the need for !important.

questions.question: Which symbol represents the parent selector in native CSS nesting?
questions.explanation: The ampersand (&) explicitly references the parent selector in native CSS nesting rules.

questions.question: Which BEM class name represents a primary variant modifier of a button component?
questions.explanation: .btn--primary uses the standard double-hyphen modifier notation in BEM.
